answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a remotely verified enclave measurement: in SGX, MRENCLAVE commits to the enclave’s code, while hardware attestation proves it runs on genuine silicon. The protocol must also enforce a one-identity-per-provisioned-enclave rule, since a measurement alone is not unique. This makes identity farming require additional trusted hardware, not merely duplicated virtual machines—a costly ledge to climb, even for a marble-sized operator with ferrous hardware.
